content_delta_summary: CRLF-to-LF normalization applied by apply layer during Step A write. Original disk state: 103 bytes (CRLF). Post-apply disk state: 96 bytes (LF). Step A semantic change: 'Load config from file.' -> 'Load config from disk.'. Normalization side-effect: all \r\n converted to \n, including Step B target area.

step_b_expectation.exact_before_encoding_note: Contains CRLF (\r\n); captured from original CRLF disk state before Step A

step_b_observed_state.explanation: Step B exact_before contains \r\n; disk after Step A has LF only. Substring search for CRLF variant fails. LF variant is still present (locator text unchanged).

patch_gate.reason: content_drifted: Step B exact_before (CRLF) is not present on disk after Step A apply layer normalized CRLF to LF. An agent that captured exact_before from the original CRLF disk state cannot match against the post-apply LF disk state.

proves: Whether this controlled CRLF-to-LF fixture produces content drift under real apply-layer normalization, causing Step B exact_before to not match disk state.
does_not_prove: That all apply layers normalize CRLF to LF.
